why.stone: Facets plus slight irregular tilts in S, 3, 8 and 5 make it feel the most like hand-hewn rock.
why.carving: The irregularity is mostly coherent, but some glyphs (lopsided 3 and 8, the skewed S) start to look wobbly rather than deliberately cut.
why.calm: Still composed at regular weight, though the unevenness adds a little restlessness.
why.personality: The rough, chipped look is unmistakable and memorable.

why.stone: Coarser, bolder facets make the display text read strongly as cut stone or an inscription.
why.carving: Facets are larger but still applied as one system and stay crisp; S and 6 become noticeably polygonal yet digits stay clearly distinguishable.
why.calm: More angular energy than K1/K4 but still steady rather than aggressive.
why.personality: Strong, unmistakable chiselled voice while keeping a classical skeleton.

why.stone: Stronger, irregular facets make it feel rough-hewn from rock, especially in the bold S and numerals.
why.carving: Facets vary in size from glyph to glyph (lumpy S, uneven 0 and 5), which edges toward broken or processed rather than one controlled chisel; digits remain legible.
why.calm: Still grounded and not shouting, but the irregular outlines make the bold numbers a bit restless.
why.personality: More rugged and memorable than K1/K4, though part of the character comes from apparent randomness.

why.stone: Looks the same as K5: irregular faceting that reads strongly as hewn stone.
why.carving: The cuts are coherent overall, but the lopsided digits and tilted S drift toward an unsteady, slightly glitchy look.
why.calm: Calm at regular weight, with mild restlessness from the irregular contours.
why.personality: A distinctive hand-chipped voice you would recognise again.

why.stone: Strong, coarse facets give a pronounced carved-stone look like K5.
why.carving: Faceting is coherent overall but some curves (S, 6, 5 bowls) turn uneven and slightly lumpy, edging toward processed rather than chiselled.
why.calm: Steady weight, though the irregular angularity adds a touch of restlessness.
why.personality: Distinct hewn character, but the irregularity reads somewhat more processed than designed.

why.stone: Strong rough faceting gives a rough-hewn rock feel, like K5.
why.carving: Irregular facet sizes on S, 0 and 5 read partly as processing artefacts rather than deliberate cuts, though the design is applied to every glyph and digits stay clear.
why.calm: Grounded with presence, slightly restless in the bold set numbers.
why.personality: Rugged and recognisable, essentially the same voice as K5.

why.stone: Coarse straight facets on every curve make the titles and numbers read clearly as chiselled stone on a classical serif skeleton.
why.carving: Faceting is applied consistently to every glyph with clean straight cuts; the narrow hexagonal 0 still separates from the wider O, though bowls are slightly mechanical.
why.calm: Regular-weight titles stay quiet and steady, and the bold set numbers have presence without shouting.
why.personality: The polygonal bowls give a recognisable inscriptional voice, though it feels uniformly processed rather than hand-cut.

why.stone: Moderate polygonal faceting on curves gives the display text a clearly hewn, inscribed feel without losing the classical serif base.
why.carving: Facets are applied consistently across letters and digits and read as deliberate cuts; 3/8 and 0/O stay distinct, though some bowls (S, 6) look slightly lumpy at the largest size.
why.calm: Regular weight stays quiet and steady; the bold has presence without shouting.
why.personality: The chiselled facets give a recognisable voice beyond a stock serif.

why.stone: Faceted bowls and flat-cut curves in a classical serif read clearly as a cut inscription without losing the serif's dignity.
why.carving: Facets are applied evenly across lower case, capitals and digits so it reads as one design, and 1/7, 3/8, 0/O stay distinct, though at the largest size some facets look more polygon-sampled than chiselled.
why.calm: Steady and measured with good presence; the faceting adds a slight restlessness to the bold numerals.
why.personality: A recognisable hewn-serif voice, but close to its siblings and to its smooth source.

why.stone: Practically the same coarse faceting as K1, so it reads as hewn stone in the same way.
why.carving: Facets are consistent and clean across the alphabet and digits; 0/O and 3/8 stay distinct.
why.calm: Steady regular titles and confident bold numbers, not aggressive.
why.personality: A distinct faceted voice, slightly mechanical in its regularity.

why.stone: Visible faceting on bowls and terminals reads as chiselled stone, very close to K1.
why.carving: Coherent, crisp facets across letters and numerals; digits remain easy to separate, with only minor unevenness on S and 6.
why.calm: Steady and grounded; the angularity adds presence without aggression.
why.personality: Distinct hewn character that would be recognised again.

why.stone: Same clear faceted-curve treatment as K1, giving a convincing cut-stone reading at title sizes.
why.carving: Consistent facets across all glyphs with crisp corners and unambiguous digits, though the large bowls still look slightly polygonal rather than V-cut.
why.calm: Steady with presence; facets add mild visual energy without aggression.
why.personality: Distinct hewn character, practically indistinguishable from K1.

why.stone: Finer, smaller facets suggest carving only when you look closely; at a glance it reads mostly as a smooth serif.
why.carving: Subtle cuts are crisp and coherent across letters and digits, with no broken shapes, but the effect is faint.
why.calm: Very calm and even, while the bold weights still carry presence.
why.personality: A slight hint of character on top of what is mostly a familiar book serif.

why.stone: Faceting is fine-grained, so the text reads mostly as a smooth serif with only a faint hewn quality.
why.carving: Cuts are clean and coherent but so subtle they barely register as carving at display size; digits are fully legible.
why.calm: Very calm and composed, with enough weight in the bold to hold presence.
why.personality: Hard to tell from the plain serif except on close inspection; character is understated.

why.stone: Only a light hint of faceting on curves, so it reads mostly as a polished book serif with a faint chiselled edge.
why.carving: Coherent and clean but so subtle at display size that the cuts read as slight low-resolution flattening rather than deliberate chisel strokes.
why.calm: Very calm and composed while the bold weights still carry presence.
why.personality: A small step away from a generic serif; easy to mistake for the uncarved face.
